subject: 🏃 Thursday — 6 mi Steady Base (Wk 1)
html:
Tomorrow: 6 mi Steady Base — 8:30–8:45 pace

First pure base run of the V6 plan. The purpose is aerobic development at a controlled intensity — not a tempo effort, not a progression. Hold 8:30–8:45 the whole way. If you feel great at mile 4 and want to push, don't. That energy is banked for Sunday's 8-mile long run.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg) → banded lateral walks (10 each direction) → glute bridges (10 reps) → quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side, PT-prescribed).

Route suggestion: Sawyer Camp Trail or Bayfront — flat enough to hold steady pace without elevation forcing you above target HR. Aim for avg HR in the 140–150 range given your recent data.

Focus cue: Hip extension, not knee drive. Think about pushing the ground behind you rather than lifting your knees forward. This loads your glutes (which need the work per PT findings) and takes stress off the patellofemoral joint. Quiet, compact stride.

Context: Week 1 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation & Durability — 80 days to race day. You're 3 for 3 on knee readings at 1/5 this week (Tuesday track, Wednesday heavy strength, both clean). Yesterday's squat session at 155 lb went well with no knee noise — your structure is handling load. This easy-day run between two strength days is intentional spacing: it flushes yesterday's lifting byproducts without adding eccentric stress.

Prep tonight: Hydrate well — you lifted heavy today and need to replace fluid. Lay out your run kit and set a 5:30 AM alarm to beat the morning warmth. Light dinner with carbs (rice bowl, pasta) to top off glycogen. Bed by 10.
